title: Applying for Study and Work: CVs and Interviews
summary: Applying to institutions and for bursaries, writing a curriculum vitae and cover letter, preparing for interviews, and presenting yourself professionally online and in person.

items: Check each institution's **closing dates**, **APS** and **subject requirements**.
Apply online (or through the Central Applications Office for KwaZulu-Natal institutions) using your Grade 11 results.
Apply for **NSFAS** and bursaries at the same time.
Keep certified copies of your ID, results and proof of income ready.

rows: Name, contact number, email, location (ID number and photo are optional)
Two or three sentences about your strengths and goals
School, highest grade passed, subjects and achievements
Part-time jobs, volunteering, holiday work, leadership roles
Computer skills, languages, driver's licence, other abilities
Two people (not family) who can vouch for you, with contact details and permission

notes.label: CV tips
notes.text: Keep it to one or two pages, use a clear layout, check spelling, tailor it to each job, use a professional email address, and never include false information.

notes.title: Improving a CV line
notes.answer: 'Sales assistant, Mokoena Stores (2024–2025): handled the till and helped increase weekend sales.'

notes.text: A **cover letter** (motivational letter) accompanies your CV. It names the position, explains why you are interested and suitable, and asks for an interview. Keep it formal and to one page.

rows: Research the organisation; prepare answers; plan your route; prepare neat clothes and documents
Arrive early; greet politely; make eye contact; listen carefully; give examples; ask a question at the end
Thank the interviewers; send a short thank-you email; reflect on what went well

notes.text: Common questions: 'Tell us about yourself', 'Why do you want this position?', 'What are your strengths and weaknesses?', 'Describe a time you solved a problem.' Use the **STAR** method: **S**ituation, **T**ask, **A**ction, **R**esult.

notes.label: Digital footprint
notes.text: Employers and bursary providers may check your social media. Remove inappropriate posts and keep a professional profile.

notes.title: Answering 'Tell me about yourself'
notes.problem: How do you answer this interview question?
steps: Keep it short and relevant to the job.
Cover present, past and why you want the role.
notes.answer: A brief summary of studies, experience and fit.

questions.prompt: What does CV stand for? (two words)
Who should you list as a reference on a CV?
options: A teacher or employer who knows your work

questions.prompt: In the STAR method for interviews, what does the A stand for?
It is acceptable to exaggerate your marks on a CV to improve your chances.
Match each item to the CV section where it belongs.
Name THREE things a cover letter should include.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): the position applied for; where you saw it; why you are interested; why you are suitable; request for an interview; formal greeting and closing

questions.prompt: Describe THREE ways to prepare for an interview.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): research the organisation; practise answers; plan route and arrive early; prepare neat clothing; bring documents; prepare questions to ask

questions.prompt: Use the STAR method to answer: 'Describe a time you showed leadership.'
questions.memo:
✓ Situation described (1)
✓ Task/challenge explained (1)
✓ Action taken by you (1)
✓ Result/outcome (1)

questions.prompt: Why should job seekers manage their social media profiles?
questions.memo:
✓ Employers may check social media before hiring (1)
✓ Inappropriate posts can cost you an opportunity (1)

questions.prompt: Name TWO documents you need when applying to a university.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): certified ID copy; Grade 11 results / matric results; proof of income (for funding); application fee proof
